definitions.explanation: Expresses the speaker's intention or plan to do something.
Indicates what the speaker believes or assumes to be the case (sometimes contrary to reality).

examples.japanese: {来年|らいねん}{日本|にほん}に{行|い}くつもりです。
examples.english: I plan to go to Japan next year.

examples.japanese: {手伝|てつだ}うつもりだったんですが...
ちゃんとやったつもりです。
examples.english: I believe I did it properly.
examples.notes: Expressing belief about one's own action

examples.japanese: {来月|らいげつ}{引|ひ}っ{越|こ}すつもりだったけど、{予定|よてい}が{変|か}わった。
examples.english: I was planning to move next month, but my plans changed.

examples.japanese: {若|わか}いつもりでも、{体|からだ}は{正直|しょうじき}です。
examples.english: Even if you think you're young, your body is honest.
examples.notes: Xのつもり = believing oneself to be X

examples.japanese: {説明|せつめい}したつもりだったのに、{全然|ぜんぜん}{伝|つた}わっていなかった。
examples.english: I thought I had explained it, but it didn't get through at all.

notes: つもり follows the plain form of verbs to express intention: 行くつもり (intend to go), 行かないつもり (intend not to go). Can also express one's belief or self-assessment: Aのつもり (I think/believe I am A). The kanji {積|つ}もり exists but hiragana is standard. Compare with {予定|よてい} (scheduled plan).
